key_insight: ZipMap is a stateful feed-forward 3D reconstruction model that replaces expensive pairwise multi-image operations with an updatable scene state, delivering linear-time, bidirectional reconstructions while using test-time training to retain or improve quality over quadratic-cost transformer methods.
problem_solved: Removes the quadratic computational scaling of state-of-the-art transformer-based multi-view methods (which become impractical for large image collections) and the quality loss seen in lightweight sequential-reconstruction approaches.
method: Stateful feed-forward architecture that maintains a compact, updatable scene representation as new images arrive, avoiding pairwise attention between all image pairs.
Linear-time aggregation: per-image updates scale linearly with the number of inputs, enabling efficient processing of large image sets without sacrificing bidirectional reconstruction capability.
Test-time training: lightweight, on-scene adaptation to refine geometry and appearance so the model matches or surpasses higher-cost baselines.
impact: Enables scalable, high-quality 3D reconstruction for large image collections or streaming scenarios, reducing compute and latency for practitioners building neural reconstruction, mapping, or AR/robotics systems.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing an updatable scene state with per-image feed-forward updates vs. a quadratic attention graph

paper_title: ZipMap: Linear-Time Stateful 3D Reconstruction with Test-Time Training
paper_authors: Haian Jin, Rundi Wu, Tianyuan Zhang, Ruiqi Gao, Jonathan T. Barron
